title: Pressure-induced self-doping and Fermi surface reconstruction in UAs2
authors: Zhenchao Wu, Yingying Cao, Yi-feng Yang
abstract: Superconductivity has recently been reported in the heavy-fermion compound UAs2 under pressure, with the highest Tc among uranium-based correlated 5f-electron superconductors. To elucidate its microscopic origin, we investigate its electronic structure using density functional theory combined with dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT). At ambient pressure, our calculations reproduce the characteristic Kondo-lattice electronic structure, with flat hybridization bands near the Fermi energy around the Γ and M points, in good agreement with angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). Under pressure, we find a systematic transfer of electrons from the more localized 5f5/2 orbitals to the more itinerant 5f7/2 orbitals, while the total U-5f occupancy remains nearly unchanged. This orbital-selective charge redistribution constitutes a pressure-induced self-doping effect that drives the 5f5/2 electrons from a localized Kondo regime toward a mixed-valence regime with enhanced charge fluctuations, leading to a dramatic reconstruction of the low-energy electronic structure. Remarkably, superconductivity emerges in the pressure range where the Fermi surface consists of two disconnected sheets with enhanced nesting, but disappears when they bend and merge into a corrugated three-dimensional cylinder. Our results provide an electronic-structure basis for understanding superconductivity in UAs2 and suggest that Fermi-surface nesting and charge fluctuations may contribute to the enhanced superconducting Tc, pointing to a possible distinction from conventional heavy-fermion superconductors.
summary: This work uses DFT+DMFT to investigate how pressure alters the electronic structure of the heavy-fermion superconductor UAs2. The key finding is that a pressure-induced self-doping effect, involving electron transfer between different 5f orbitals, reconstructs the Fermi surface into a state conducive to high Tc superconductivity. This suggests that orbital physics and Fermi surface nesting are crucial ingredients for unconventional pairing in correlated materials.
main_problem: To elucidate the microscopic origin of superconductivity in UAs2 under pressure by understanding how electronic structure changes drive superconducting behavior.
main_result: Superconductivity emerges when the Fermi surface has two disconnected, nested sheets, driven by a pressure-induced self-doping effect involving orbital-selective charge redistribution between 5f orbitals.
method: Density Functional Theory combined with Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DFT+DMFT) calculations were used to model the electronic structure evolution under varying pressures.
model_or_system: The study focuses on UAs2, a heavy-fermion compound exhibiting superconductivity. The theoretical framework models the correlated 5f electrons using DFT+DMFT, incorporating spin-orbit coupling and local Coulomb interactions.
key_observables: Momentum-resolved spectral function A(k, omega), Partial Densities of States (DOS) for U-5f orbitals, Fermi surface topology, and superconducting transition temperature (Tc).
important_parameters: Pressure range (ambient to 45 GPa); orbital indices ($j=5/2$ vs $j=7/2$); charge fluctuation probabilities.
main_assumptions: The calculations assume a nonmagnetic state for simplicity, and the mechanism remains partially unexplained despite strong evidence pointing toward nesting and fluctuations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram showing structural transitions (tetragonal to orthorhombic) alongside electronic structure changes; spectral functions show flat bands shifting with pressure, and Fermi surface plots detail the evolution from disconnected sheets to a merged cylinder.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the ambient pressure state matching ARPES data. It then analyzes the effect of increasing pressure, detailing orbital-selective charge transfer (self-doping), followed by mapping how the resulting Fermi surface topology dictates the superconducting phase boundary.
why_interesting: While focused on actinides, the concept of tuning electronic correlations via external parameters (pressure) to induce novel quantum states like high-$T_c$ superconductivity through orbital physics is highly relevant to understanding strongly correlated systems in AMO and condensed matter theory.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Schematic phase diagram and crystal structures of UAs2 reproduced from Ref. [20]. The upper panel shows the tetragonal and orthorhombic crystal structures together with their corresponding Brillouin zones in the low- and high- pressure phases, respectively. The lower panel presents the schematic pressure–temperature phase diagram below 40 K, showing the low-pressure antiferromagnetic (AFM) phase, the superconducting (SC) dome, the non-Fermi-liquid (NFL) re- gion above Tc, and the high-pressure Fermi-liquid (FL) regime reported only up to 40.5 GPa. The yellow shaded region indicates the pressure range over which the tetragonal-to- orthorhombic structural transition occurs.

FIG. 4: (a) Evolution of the Fermi surfaces at 26.8, 30.8, and 45 GPa. (b) Log-log plots of the negative imaginary part of the Matsubara self-energy for the U-5f5/2 states. The solid lines are power-law fits to the data at 26.8, 30.8, and 45 GPa, while the green and purple dashed lines denote the reference power laws with exponents of 0.5, characteristic of non-Fermi-liquid behavior, and 1, expected for a Fermi liquid, respectively. The Fermi-surface visualization was performed using the FermiSurfer code [42]. The colors represent the magnitudes of the Fermi velocity.
